result.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
result.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

AI.brief_summary: 这篇 102 页综述以「世界建模」为统一视角，把观测视频视为潜在时序世界的有损部分投影，按 reading（推断世界属性）、writing（条件生成视频）、sharing（理解与生成共享机制）、interacting（在动作与观测下预测和更新状态）四类操作梳理任务、表示、模型、数据与基准，并提炼开放挑战。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属视频/世界模型领域，但其「序列时序连贯 vs 潜在世界状态一致」的区分，以及强调持续状态、可控演化与基于交互和下游决策的评价，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载证据与状态更新的评测提供概念线索，可供核查。
